name: rain_torus_w0

geometry.kind: sink (2) where x % 3 == 1 and y % 3 == 1, source (1) elsewhere

stimulus.click: a click is a rain at the nearest source cell (mu_rain for rain_dur ticks)

niche_choice: Numbers fixed before any organism lives here. Timescales: rain (50 ticks) << food lifetime (500 ticks) << richness drift (2000 ticks, as W2); rich and lean times vary at random (user's choice, 2026-10-26). Rain rate and size by three principles, judged with ideal policies only (scripts/witness/nested_niche_sweep.py, results nested_niche_sweep_final_20261027.json): (1) feasible: the best local forager (senses only its own cell; memory time constant 1-30 ticks and speed 1-10 cells per tick, the best counts) eats on average >= f* = 10, the maintenance threshold of the body (under mass action intake is proportional to the food under the body and the reserve smooths a few hundred ticks, so the mean food counts, not the time above f*); (2) sensing useful: a blind walker eats less than half of that; (3) leanest: least standing food among those. Chosen: rain_rate 0.001 per tick per world, mu_rain 25 (~13,000 quanta per rain): world mean food 4.7, best local forager 13.3, blind 4.1. Small frequent rains failed (a blind walker catches up as rain grows); faster diffusion or longer food life flatten the field and failed too. Never tuned on an organism's result.
notes: Everything the world does is a rule of the Lean table: rain, drying and waste removal are exchanges with the outer reservoir at the stimulus potential (supply rule), spreading is the diffusion rule; the simulator computes their rates from the same formulas (gate check nested_world_rates_match_lean).
dissolution: physics (2026-10-27, after G26c and frees_only_by_dissolving): a body without intact membrane dissolves into the cell's waste pool with everything it holds (B plus inner content); conductance is symmetric Metropolis, kappa_dis * exp(-|dE|/2), so downhill dissolution runs at kappa_dis = 0.005 (a corpse lasts ~200 ticks) and the reverse (a dead body forming from waste) at kappa_dis * exp(-|dE|). B = 16; the reverse is negligible at the waste levels of this world (simulators omit it; the cross-check reports the bound).
food_energy: physics (2026-10-27): a food quantum carries chemical energy foodE = 8 relative to a waste quantum (food is free energy, not only matter; derived earlier for the 2D world, forgotten in the first nested table). The food reservoir potentials shift by +8 (dry 0, rain 16), so the world's own dynamics are unchanged; only the organism's food and waste exchanges see the difference. Without it food and waste were the same content at different concentrations and bodies condensed out of concentrated waste.
mass_action: physics (2026-10-27, system map 7.1, Lean poolFactor / mass_action_up/down): every pool change carries the conductance sqrt(product of multiplicities), so a pool of n quanta gains one at a rate proportional to V - n and loses one at a rate proportional to n; each quantum moves on its own. The first table used a constant conductance (the pool acted as one unit: decay and diffusion per quantum fell as 1/sqrt(n), halos stayed narrow and uptake grew as sqrt(food)). Constants re-declared from the same timescales, not from any organism: a dry food quantum lives 500 ticks (kappa_in * exp(foodE/2) = 1/500, so kappa_in = e^-4/500); a rain fills an empty cell at ~5 quanta per tick (kappa_in * V * exp((mu_rain - foodE)/2) = 5, so mu_rain = 17); a quantum hops 0.1 per tick to each neighbour (2 kappa_diff V = 0.1), so a food patch spreads over sqrt(D tau) ~ 7 cells: wider than one cell (a gradient exists) and much narrower than the torus (patches stay separate). Waste leaves a sink at the same 1/500 per quantum (mu_sink = -8).
